html:
The Arab Spring was a wave of protests and uprisings that swept much of the Arab world in 2010 to 2012. It began in Tunisia in December 2010, when a street vendor, Mohamed Bouazizi, set himself on fire after police seized his cart.

Behind the anger were old rulers, police abuse, corruption, high food prices and young people without jobs. Satellite TV and social media spread the news fast. Protesters chanted "the people want the fall of the regime".

  • Tunisia: President Ben Ali fled in January 2011; the country became a democracy for a decade.
  • Egypt: Hosni Mubarak fell after 18 days of protest in Tahrir Square. The Muslim Brotherhood won elections, then the army took power again in 2013.
  • Libya: a civil war, with NATO air strikes, ended in the killing of Gaddafi.
  • Syria: crackdown turned into the Syrian civil war.
  • Yemen: President Saleh left, and civil war followed.
  • Bahrain: protests were crushed with Saudi help.

Outside Tunisia, the hopes mostly ended in new dictatorship or war, and in mass flight such as the Syrian refugee crisis.
sum: The Arab Spring was a wave of protests and uprisings that swept much of the Arab world in 2010 to 2012. It began in Tunisia in December 2010, when a street vendor, Mohamed Bouazizi, set himself on fire after police seized his cart.
